newsitem.title: BRAZIL: USDA highlights Brazil coffee crop division - trade.
newsitem.headline: USDA highlights Brazil coffee crop division - trade.

text.p: Conflicting forecasts within the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) of Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop show even the USDA is divided over the size of the harvest this year, Brazilian traders said.
"I guess it shows that like everyone else, people in the USDA have different ideas," one trader said.
The official USDA estimate was issued on June 13 and plotted Brazil 1997/98 coffee output at 28 million bags, up from 27.5 million bags in 1996/97.

This caused an outcry within Brazil for two reasons. Firstly the actual size of the estimate conflicted with most trade views of 23 million to 25 million bags and a government forecast of 22 million bags.
Secondly, the suggestion that this year's harvest was bigger - albeit marginally - than last year's was unprecedented.

Today a field report written by a U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo and dated May 12 was made public in which the attache plotted the 1997/98 harvest at 24 million bags versus 27.5 million bags the previous year.
Brazilian coffee traders, amazed by the report, also welcomed what they regarded as a more realistic forecast for this harvest and also the acknowledgement that the crop would be down on last year.

"It is impossible to have a number "x" (for 1996/97), say 27.5 million bags, and then say that this year's crop is higher. This (the attache) report makes sense," said Jorge Esteve, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Association which also sees the 1997/98 crop at 24 million bags.
"Around 24 million bags is the number that we all expect. Everyone knows that this harvest we will not be harvesting 28 million bags," said Jair Coser, president of leading coffee exporter Unicafe.

There is one other person however who is said to see a 1997/98 crop of over 28 million bags - Leon Yallouz, the former USDA coffee agronomist in Brazil who since last year has been providing private estimates to clients.
His latest forecast, said to have been for 28.6 million bags, was released shortly after the official USDA estimate.
"When Yallouz's figure came out right after the USDA, everyone said Yallouz is still working for the USDA. Now we have the confirmation," one trader said.
When asked to comment on the attache report today Yallouz said he did not agree with the figure for 1997/98.

As far as 1996/97 production was concerned, Yallouz said that 27.5 million bags was his last estimate of the 1996/97 crop while working for the USDA. But he declined to say if this was still his personal working estimate.
When asked to comment on the official USDA figure of 28 million bags, Yallouz said he had not seen the figure formally and so could not pass judgement.
This is not the first time there has been confusion over USDA figures.

In December last year, another attache report from Sao Paulo was released in Washington containing an estimate for the 1996/97 crop of 25.8 million bags which conflicted with an official forecast the previous week of 27 million bags.
As was the case last year, the current apparent lack of consensus within the USDA has done much to damage the entity's credibility, traders said.
And the question still remains - what is the size of the 1997/98 crop?

Brazilian trader Tristao has recently raised its own forecast of the 1997/98 crop to 25.6 million bags from an April figure of 23.5 million, citing favorable climatic conditions, careful treatment and higher than expected yields.
On the other hand, producers are talking about revising down their estimates because of the recent rains which have dashed coffee to the ground, some of which could be lost.
The Brazilian government is working on introducing a new crop forecasting system which should be in place for 1998/99.

But at present the total range of estimates for 1997/98 runs from 18 million bags to in excess of 28 million bags - a range which, as one analyst pointed out, represents around 10 percent of global supply in 1997/98.
((-Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
